headlineClaims.title: Start macOS compile admission beside the fast Linux jobs
headlineClaims.metric: run start to compile admission job created
headlineClaims.population: pull_request ci.yml runs, first attempts
headlineClaims.note: 160.5 s to 39.5 s median; p90 236 s to 77.5 s. One late-night hour after merge; re-measure on a weekday.

headlineClaims.title: Prune expired R2 cache archives, never one a latest pointer names
headlineClaims.metric: R2 cache bytes deleted by the first prune
headlineClaims.population: manaflow-ai/cmux CI cache bucket
headlineClaims.note: One-time reclaim. The steady-state effect is capping growth at about one day of per-commit archives, not measured here.

headlineClaims.title: Seed DerivedData on the 12 vCPU macOS 26 pool
headlineClaims.population: seed-derived-data.yml runs on main
headlineClaims.note: 1,342 s to 16 s median. After 14:00Z the 12 vCPU pool queued too (621 s and 663 s), once PR admissions began preferring it.

headlineClaims.title: Build focused runs from compile admission's DerivedData seed
headlineClaims.metric: E2E app build step on 6 vCPU macOS 26
headlineClaims.population: Focused test-e2e.yml builds with a seed hit
headlineClaims.note: 1,021 s to 435 s median.

headlineClaims.title: Start macOS checkouts from main's git objects
headlineClaims.metric: compile admission checkout plus git seed restore
headlineClaims.population: macOS compile admission
headlineClaims.note: 48 s median to 12 s (4 s checkout plus 8 s restore). One after-sample per lane.

headlineClaims.title: Restore SwiftPM's manifest cache for package resolves
headlineClaims.population: macOS 26 compile admissions
headlineClaims.note: 63 s to 17 s median.

headlineClaims.title: Seed each Swift job width admission compiles at
headlineClaims.metric: SwiftEmitModule tasks in the cmux scheme of a test-only seeded admission
headlineClaims.measurementWindow: one admission before (run 36040706124) and one after (run 36077356582), both 6 vCPU
headlineClaims.population: Seeded macOS compile admissions on Blacksmith macOS 26 pools
headlineClaims.note: 62 to 0, one run each. Holds when a seed of the runner's width exists. Owned 14-CPU minis have none yet (cmuxterm-hq#590). cmuxTests still recompiles fully after adoption (cmux#14320).

headlineClaims.title: Keep the runner account out of the SwiftPM manifest cache key
headlineClaims.metric: admission Resolve Swift packages step on owned minis
headlineClaims.population: Compile admissions on owned glaeda minis
headlineClaims.note: 52 to 56 s before, 13 to 16 s after; 36 s is the conservative gap (52 minus 16). cli-pipe-regressions on a mini still missed (41 s, n=1) because its workspace path differs.

headlineClaims.title: Measure the fleet compilation cache mini to mini on the full cmux app
headlineClaims.metric: fresh full cmux app build with a filled fleet cache
headlineClaims.measurementWindow: one cold and one cached build, 2026-09-24
headlineClaims.population: Fresh builds on a Manaflow M4 Pro mini
headlineClaims.note: 756 s to 132 s. Lab measurement, not CI. For the full app the store and reader were on the same mini; cross-machine was shown on the CmuxSettingsUI chain, and for the full app in glaeda-1180.

headlineClaims.title: Run the CmuxMobileShell package tests serially
headlineClaims.population: 1,060 CmuxMobileShell package tests
headlineClaims.note: Parallel execution exceeded 12 minutes without finishing; serial execution completed in 65 seconds. The stored 655-second reduction is therefore a lower bound.

headlineClaims.title: Move focused E2E dispatches to the low-queue macOS pool
headlineClaims.population: 33 macOS 15 and 25 macOS 26 focused E2E dispatches
headlineClaims.note: Observed queue p90 was 83.3 minutes on macOS 15 and 1.0 minute on macOS 26. Execution median was about four minutes slower on macOS 26, and the test mixes differed, so the comparison is operational rather than causal.

headlineClaims.title: Read app-host artifacts over parallel range requests
headlineClaims.population: Seven app-host product consumers in a full-suite run
headlineClaims.note: The baseline was about eight minutes per consumer; the PR reports the transfer step as roughly 98 percent transport time and moves the path to concurrent ranges with verification and fallback.

headlineClaims.title: Throttle push-triggered Nightly builds by published commit age
headlineClaims.population: push-triggered Nightly publication work
headlineClaims.note: The PR projects roughly 450–600 macOS minutes/day avoided at the two-hour default. This record stores the lower edge of that stated range; the PR also gives a roughly 280-minute/day lower-bound scenario.

headlineClaims.title: Measure CI waste on a schedule
headlineClaims.measurementWindow: first real report, approximately 23.1 hours of a 24-hour window
headlineClaims.population: 2,424 workflow/head pairs in the fetched run set
headlineClaims.note: The report found 9,763 runs beyond the first for a head that did not change. This is an observation to investigate, not a claim that every repeated run is removable.

headlineClaims.title: Remove full-history checkout and unconditional Zig setup from iOS uploads
headlineClaims.measurementWindow: real upload baseline plus local shallow-checkout timing
headlineClaims.population: iOS TestFlight/App Store upload runs when the pinned GhosttyKit prebuilt exists
headlineClaims.note: The PR states about 16–17 macOS minutes saved per upload. This record stores the lower edge of that range.

headlineClaims.title: Measure CMUX macOS CI capacity and replacement-cost exposure
headlineClaims.population: All 1,966,401 self-hosted macOS minutes priced at WarpBuild's cheapest documented 6-vCPU macOS rate
headlineClaims.note: Floor valuation only: 655,467 equivalent minutes per 30 days at $0.08/min. No 12-vCPU premium is applied. This is replacement-cost exposure, not a claim that every minute was actually billed to Warp or saved by one contributor.

headlineClaims.title: Compile the E2E test product once and reuse it on reruns
headlineClaims.population: Reruns of a failed focused E2E dispatch while the retained product remains available
headlineClaims.note: Fresh dispatches do not claim lower total runner minutes; this figure is the measured compile portion removed from a rerun by the new job split.

headlineClaims.title: Report recorded failures even when app-host results are incomplete
headlineClaims.population: Recorded XCTest and Swift Testing failures in the incomplete app-host shards
headlineClaims.note: The fix changes diagnostics, not the fail-closed verdict: incomplete runs remain failed while recorded failures are now named.

headlineClaims.title: Seed the test compilation cache from one clean build
headlineClaims.population: pull requests restoring the shared test compilation-cache seed
headlineClaims.note: The clean seed is about 3.5 GiB instead of roughly 5.0 GiB, so every pull request restores about 1.5 GiB less.

headlineClaims.title: Debounce macOS admission on superseded pull-request pushes
headlineClaims.population: Superseded pull-request runs that would otherwise start macOS work
headlineClaims.note: Replay estimate at the default 180-second delay; the same analysis measured a 1.4-minute median increase to the green signal.

headlineClaims.title: Route pull-request macOS jobs to sponsored capacity
headlineClaims.population: Pull-request macOS overflow work in the sampled CMUX CI day
headlineClaims.note: This moves workload onto sponsored capacity; it does not claim the compute disappeared.

headlineClaims.title: Trigger the persistent Mac router once per CI run
headlineClaims.population: persistent-macos-router workflow invocations
headlineClaims.note: The measured baseline was about 6,864 router runs/day; the once-per-CI-run trigger was expected to produce about 1,253/day, an 82% reduction.

headlineClaims.title: Seed compilation cache on the runner pull requests restore from
headlineClaims.population: Pull-request admission before the cache producer and consumer runner layouts matched
headlineClaims.note: The PR explicitly left warm compile time unmeasured until the next scheduled seed.

headlineClaims.title: Move Computer Use runtime out of the 3,700-file app module
headlineClaims.population: comment-only edit to AgentPIDProcessIdentity.swift before and after moving it from the app target to CmuxFoundation
headlineClaims.note: The measured build fell from 38.9 seconds to 13.3 seconds and compiled zero app-target Swift files after the move.

headlineClaims.title: Reuse one warm DerivedData across development tags
headlineClaims.population: new development tag at the same commit after a warm build
headlineClaims.note: Fresh DerivedData took 953 seconds; a new tag using the already-warm shared DerivedData took 35.7 seconds.

headlineClaims.title: Stop pull requests from evicting shared cache seeds
headlineClaims.population: 27 GitHub cache entries visible to the repository
headlineClaims.note: The oldest macOS entry was only five minutes old and the shared Debug compilation seed was already missing. Pull-request jobs had 14 save+restore cache steps and wrote 1–3 GB PR-scoped entries.

headlineClaims.title: Seed the Debug compilation cache from main
headlineClaims.population: macOS compile admission from an empty compilation cache
headlineClaims.note: The PR deliberately did not quote an unmeasured CI savings number before the scheduled seed had run.

headlineClaims.title: Parallelize slow and history-dependent CI guards
headlineClaims.population: Linux guard path gating macOS admission
headlineClaims.note: Measured guard wall time fell from 385.5 seconds to 124.3 seconds, about a 68% reduction.

accountingRule: Only claims explicitly marked additive are summed. Baselines, capacity shifts, overlapping savings, and projections stay separate.
